title: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Tax, Super, and minimum wage nz Context
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our guide. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and minimum wage nz comparisons for Australian workers.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For full-time work, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,269 annual gross. This is before tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award. Most workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates, including penalty rates and allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on ordinary earnings including the loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For a full-time employee, the typical assumption is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. However, if you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. This gives you the gross amount before tax, Medicare, and super. For the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week gives a weekly gross of $1,004.90 ($26.44 × 38) and an annual gross of approximately $52,269 ($1,004.90 × 52). This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. If you are paid a salary, you can reverse the formula to find your equivalent hourly rate: salary ÷ (hours per week × 52).

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply double your weekly pay. Using the National Minimum Wage example, your fortnightly gross would be $2,009.80. This is a useful figure for budgeting and comparing with job advertisements that quote fortnightly salaries. Some employers pay monthly, in which case you can multiply your weekly pay by 4.33 (since there are 52 weeks in 12 months) to get a monthly estimate.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award that sets higher minimum rates, including penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award have specific rates for different classifications. If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a casual loading of 25% on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. Remember, superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, including the casual loading if it is part of your ordinary hours. Always check your award or agreement to ensure you are receiving the correct rate.

### Casual Loading and Super

When using the timesheet on this site, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool will calculate it for you. Superannuation guarantee contributions are calculated on your ordinary time earnings, which include the casual loading if it is paid for all ordinary hours. The super rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a casual worker on the National Minimum Wage with loading, ordinary earnings are $33.05 per hour, so weekly ordinary earnings are $1,255.90, and super would be $150.71 per week ($1,255.90 × 12%). This super is paid on top of your wages, not deducted from them.

### Average Weekly Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages across all industries and states, not medians for a specific job. Your own pay may differ based on your award, experience, and location. For a more tailored comparison, refer to [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Ordinary-time earnings vary across Australian states and territories due to differences in industry composition, cost of living, and local labour markets. For instance, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales and Victoria tend to be higher than in Tasmania or South Australia, reflecting the concentration of high-paying industries such as mining and professional services in certain regions. The ABS publishes state-level averages, but these are broad figures. If you are comparing a job offer in a different state, consider the local award rates and the cost of living. The National Minimum Wage applies nationwide, but award rates can have state-specific variations. For example, some awards have different rates for employees in remote areas or specific regions. Always check the relevant award or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your situation.

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200; 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% on income above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners based on the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage earning $52,269, the tax would be approximately $5,092 (using the 2026-27 rates: $0 on first $18,200; $4,020 on $18,201 to $45,000; $2,172 on $45,001 to $52,269; total $6,192). Medicare levy at 2% = $1,045, total tax and Medicare ~$7,237. This is an estimate; your actual tax may vary depending on deductions and offsets. This estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

### Comparing with minimum wage nz

If you are considering work across the Tasman, you may be interested in the minimum wage nz. New Zealand sets its own minimum wage rates, which are different from Australia's. While this article focuses on Australian pay, you can use the same conversion formula for New Zealand dollars if you know the hourly rate. For the most current New Zealand minimum wage, check the New Zealand government's official website. Remember that tax rates, superannuation (KiwiSaver), and cost of living differ between the two countries. The formula remains the same: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For example, if New Zealand's minimum wage is, say, NZ$23 per hour (hypothetical), working 40 hours per week would give an annual gross of NZ$47,840. However, we do not have official figures here; always refer to the New Zealand government for accurate rates.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on the formula hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For a personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/) on this site, where you can enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

For more detailed information, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.
